cues.en: I've got several fun things for you this video, an unsolved problem, a very elegant solution to a weaker version of the problem, and a little bit about what topology is and why people care.
cues.zh: 这期视频我给大家准备了几个有趣的东西：一个未解决的问题、这个问题弱化版本的一个非常优雅的解法，还有一点关于拓扑学是什么、以及人们为什么关心它的内容。

cues.en: But before I jump into it, it's worth saying a few words on why I'm excited to share this solution.
cues.zh: 不过在开始之前，我想先说说为什么我很兴奋能分享这个解决方案。

cues.en: When I was a kid, since I loved math and sought out various mathy things, I would occasionally find myself in some talk or a seminar where people wanted to get the youth excited about things that mathematicians
cues.zh: 小时候，因为我热爱数学并且四处搜寻各种数学相关的东西，我偶尔会去听一些讲座或研讨会，那是人们为了激发年轻人对数学家所做的事情的热情而举办的

cues.en: care about.
cues.zh: 你在意的。

cues.en: A very common go to topic to excite our imaginations
cues.zh: 一个很常见、能激发我们想象力的话题

cues.en: was topology.
cues.zh: 拓扑结构。

cues.en: We might be shown something like a Mobius strip, maybe building it out of construction paper by twisting a rectangle and gluing its ends. Look, we'd be told as we were asked to draw a line along the surface. It's a surface with just one side.
cues.zh: 可能会给我们看类似莫比乌斯带的东西，也许是用手工纸做的，把矩形扭转后把两端粘起来。看，当我们被要求在表面上画一条线时，会被告知。这是一个只有一个面的曲面。

cues.en: Or we might be told that topologists view coffee mugs and donuts as the same thing since each has just one hole.
cues.zh: 或者我们可能听说过，拓扑学家把咖啡杯和甜甜圈看作同一样东西，因为两者都只有一个洞。

cues.en: But these kinds of demos always left a lurking question.
cues.zh: 但这种演示总留下一个挥之不去的疑问。

cues.en: How is this math? How does any of this actually help to solve problems?
cues.zh: 这跟数学有什么关系？这些到底怎么帮助解决问题？

cues.en: It wasn't until I saw the problem that I'm about to show you with its elegant and surprising solution that I started to understand why mathematicians actually care about some of these shapes and the properties they have.
cues.zh: 直到我看到我即将展示给你的这个问题，以及它优雅而令人惊讶的解法，我才开始理解为什么数学家们实际上在乎这些形状及其具有的性质。

cues.en: So there's this unsolved problem called the inscribed square problem.
cues.zh: 所以有一个未解的数学难题叫做内接正方形问题。

cues.en: If you have a closed loop, meaning you squiggle some line through space in a potentially crazy way and you end up back where you started,
cues.zh: 如果你有一个闭环，也就是说你在空间中用某种可能很疯狂的方式画一条线，最后又回到起点，

cues.en: the question is whether or not you'll always be able to find four points on this loop that make up a square.
cues.zh: 问题在于，你是否总能在这个环上找到四个点，构成一个正方形。

cues.en: If your closed loop was a circle for example, it's quite easy to find an inscribed square,
cues.zh: 比如，如果你的闭环是一个圆，那很容易找到一个内接正方形，

cues.en: infinitely many in fact.
cues.zh: 事实上，有无数个。

cues.en: If your loop was instead an ellipse, it's still pretty easy to find an inscribed square.
cues.zh: 如果你的环是一个椭圆，仍然很容易找到一个内接正方形。

cues.en: The question is whether or not every possible closed loop, no matter how crazy, has at least one inscribed square.
cues.zh: 问题在于，是否每一个可能的闭环，无论多疯狂，都至少有一个内接正方形。

cues.en: Pretty interesting. Right? I mean, just the fact that this is unsolved is interesting, that the current tools of math can neither confirm nor deny that there's some loop with no inscribed square in it.
cues.zh: 挺有意思的，对吧？我是说，光是这个问题尚未解决就很有趣了——现有的数学工具既不能证实也不能否定存在某个没有内接正方形的环。

cues.en: Now if we weaken the question a bit and ask about inscribed rectangles
cues.zh: 现在如果我们把问题稍微弱化一下，问的是内接矩形

cues.en: instead of inscribed squares,
cues.zh: 而不是内接正方形，

cues.en: it's still pretty hard, but there is a beautiful video worthy solution that might actually be my favorite piece of math.
cues.zh: 它仍然相当难，但有一个漂亮的、值得做成视频的解法，可能是我最喜欢的一段数学。

cues.en: The idea is to shift the focus away from individual points on the loop and instead onto pairs of points.
cues.zh: 思路是把焦点从环上的单个点转移到点对上。

cues.en: We'll use the following fact about rectangles.
cues.zh: 我们将用到关于矩形的以下事实。

cues.en: Let's label the vertices of some rectangle a b c d.
cues.zh: 我们把某个矩形的顶点标为 a b c d。

cues.en: Then the pair of points a c has a few things in common with the pair of points b d.
cues.zh: 那么点对 a c 和点对 b d 有一些共同之处。

cues.en: The distance between a and c equals the distance between b and d, and the midpoint of a and c is the same as the midpoint of b and d.
cues.zh: a 和 c 之间的距离等于 b 和 d 之间的距离，而且 a 和 c 的中点与 b 和 d 的中点是同一个。

cues.en: In fact, anytime you have two separate pairs of points in space, a c and b d, if you can guarantee that they share a midpoint and that the distance between a c equals the distance between b and d,
cues.zh: 事实上，只要你在空间中有两对不同的点，a c 和 b d，如果能保证它们共用一个中点，并且 a 到 c 的距离等于 b 到 d 的距离，

cues.en: it's enough to guarantee that those four points make up a rectangle.
cues.zh: 就足以保证这四个点构成一个矩形。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is try to prove that any closed loop it's always possible to find two distinct pairs of points on that loop that share a midpoint and which are the same distance apart.
cues.zh: 所以我们要做的是，尝试证明对于任何闭合环路，总能找到该环路上两对不同的点，它们共用一个中点，并且彼此距离相等。

cues.en: Take a moment to make sure that's clear. We're finding two distinct pairs of points that share a common midpoint and which are the same distance apart.
cues.zh: 花点时间确保你理解了这一点。我们要找的是两对不同的点，它们共用一个中点，并且距离相等。

cues.en: The way we'll go about this is to define a function that takes in pairs of points on the loop and outputs a single point in three d space which kind of encodes the midpoint and distance information.
cues.zh: 我们的方法是定义一个函数，输入环路上成对的点，输出三维空间中的一个点，这个点编码了中点和距离信息。

cues.en: It will be sort of like a graph.
cues.zh: 它会有点像一张图。

cues.en: Consider the closed loop to be sitting on the x y plane in three d space.
cues.zh: 把闭合环路看作位于三维空间的 x y 平面上。

cues.en: For a given pair of points, label their midpoint m which will be some point on the x y plane and label the distance between them d.
cues.zh: 对于给定的一对点，把它们的中点标记为 m，它会是 x y 平面上的某个点，并把它们之间的距离标记为 d。

cues.en: Plot the point which is exactly d units above that midpoint m in the z direction.
cues.zh: 在 z 方向上，标出恰好位于该中点 m 上方 d 个单位处的点。

cues.en: As you do this for many possible pairs of points, you'll effectively be drawing through three d space.
cues.zh: 当你对许多可能的点对这样做时，你实际上会在三维空间中画出一条轨迹。

cues.en: And if you do it for all possible pairs of points on the loop, you'll draw out some kind of surface above the plane.
cues.zh: 如果你对环路上所有可能的点对都这样做，你就会在平面上方绘制出某种曲面。

cues.en: Now look at the surface and notice how it seems to hug the loop itself.
cues.zh: 现在观察这个曲面，注意它是如何紧紧贴住这个闭环本身的。

cues.en: This is actually gonna be important later so let's think about why it happens.
cues.zh: 这实际上在后面会很重要，所以我们来思考一下为什么会这样。

cues.en: As the pair of points on the loop gets closer and closer, the plotted point gets lower since its height is by definition equal to the distance between the points.
cues.zh: 随着闭环上这对点越来越近，绘制出的点也会变低，因为根据定义，它的高度等于这两点之间的距离。

cues.en: Also, the midpoint gets closer and closer to the loop as the points approach each other.
cues.zh: 此外，随着这两个点彼此接近，它们的中点也越来越靠近这个闭环。

cues.en: Once the pair of points coincides,
cues.zh: 一旦这对点重合，

cues.en: meaning the input of our function looks like x x for some point x on the loop, the plotted point of the surface will be exactly on the loop at the point x.
cues.zh: 也就是我们函数的输入对于闭环上的某个点 x 呈现出 x x 的形式时，曲面上绘制的点就会精确落在这个闭环的点 x 上。

cues.en: Okay, so remember that. Another important fact is that this function is continuous
cues.zh: 好，记住这一点。另一个重要的事实是，这个函数是连续的，

cues.en: and all that really means is that if you slightly adjust a given pair of points then the corresponding output in three d space is only slightly adjusted as well. There's never a sudden discontinuous jump.
cues.zh: 这其实际上的意思就是，如果你稍微调整给定的这对点，那么三维空间中对应的输出也只会发生微小的调整。绝不会出现突兀的断崖式跳跃。

cues.en: Our goal then is to show that this function has a collision
cues.zh: 那么我们的目标就是证明这个函数存在碰撞，

cues.en: that two distinct pairs of points each map to the same spot in three d space
cues.zh: 即两对不同的点映射到了三维空间中的同一个位置，

cues.en: because the only way for that to happen is if they share a common midpoint and if their distance d apart from each other is the same.
cues.zh: 因为只有当它们共用同一个中点，且彼此之间的距离 d 相同时，这种情况才会发生。

cues.en: So in some sense finding an inscribed rectangle comes down to showing that this surface has to intersect itself.
cues.zh: 所以在某种意义上，寻找内接矩形归根结底就是要证明这个曲面必然会自我相交。

cues.en: To move forward from here we need to build up a relationship with the idea of pairs of points on a loop.
cues.zh: 为了从这里继续推进，我们需要建立起与闭环上点对这个概念的联系。

cues.en: Think about how we represent pairs of real numbers using a two dimensional coordinate plane.
cues.zh: 想想我们如何用二维坐标平面来表示实数对。

cues.en: Analogous to this, we're gonna seek out a certain two d surface which naturally represents all pairs of points on the loop.
cues.zh: 类似地，我们要找的是一个特定的二维曲面，它能自然地表示环上所有的点对。

cues.en: Understanding the properties of this surface will help to show why the graph that we just defined has to intersect itself.
cues.zh: 理解这个曲面的性质，将有助于说明为什么我们刚才定义的图必然会自相交。

cues.en: Now when I say pair of points, there are two things that I could be talking about.
cues.zh: 当我说“点对”时，我可能指的是两种东西。

cues.en: The first is ordered pairs of points which would mean a pair like a b would be considered distinct from the pair b a. That is, there's some notion of which point is the first one.
cues.zh: 第一种是有序点对，也就是说像 a、b 这样的对会被认为与 b、a 不同。也就是说，存在某种“哪个点是第一个”的概念。

cues.en: The second idea is unordered points, where a b and b a would be considered the same thing, where all that really matters is what the points are and there's no meaning to which one is first.
cues.zh: 第二种是无序点对，其中 a、b 和 b、a 会被视为同一回事，真正重要的只是这些点是什么，而哪个在前并没有意义。

cues.en: Ultimately,
cues.zh: 最终，

cues.en: we wanna understand unordered pairs of points, but to get there we need to take a path of thought through ordered pairs.
cues.zh: 我们想理解的是无序点对，但要达到那里，我们需要先通过有序点对来思考。

cues.en: We'll start out by straightening out the loop, cutting it at some point and deforming it into an interval.
cues.zh: 我们先把这个环拉直，在某一点处剪开，再把它变形为一个区间。

cues.en: For the sake of having some labels, let's say that this is the interval on the number line from zero to one.
cues.zh: 为了便于标记，不妨说这就是数轴上从 0 到 1 的区间。

cues.en: By following where each point ends up, every point on the loop corresponds with a unique number on this interval
cues.zh: 通过追踪每个点最终落在哪里，环上的每个点都对应这个区间上的唯一一个数，

cues.en: except for the point where the cut happened which corresponds simultaneously
cues.zh: 除了剪开的那个点，它同时对应

cues.en: to both endpoints of the interval meaning the number zero and one.
cues.zh: 区间的两个端点，也就是数 0 和 1。

cues.en: Now the benefit of straightening out this loop like this is that we can start thinking about pairs of points the same way we think about pairs of numbers.
cues.zh: 把环这样展直的好处是，我们可以像看待数对一样去看待点对。

cues.en: Make a y axis using a second interval
cues.zh: 用第二个区间画一条 y 轴

cues.en: then associate each pair of values on the interval with a single point in this one by one square that they span out.
cues.zh: 然后把区间上的每一对数值，对应到它们张成的这个单位正方形中的单个点。

cues.en: Every individual point of this square naturally corresponds to a pair of points on the loop since its x and y coordinates are each numbers between zero and one
cues.zh: 这个正方形的每个独立点都自然对应环上的一对点，因为它的 x 和 y 坐标都是 0 到 1 之间的数

cues.en: which are in turn associated to some unique point on the loop.
cues.zh: 而这些数又各自对应环上某个唯一的点。

cues.en: Remember, we're trying to find a surface that naturally represents the set of all pairs of points on the loop and this square is the first step to doing that.
cues.zh: 记住，我们要找一个能自然表示环上所有点对的曲面，而这个正方形就是第一步。

cues.en: The problem is that there's some ambiguity when it comes to the edges of the square.
cues.zh: 问题在于正方形的边缘存在一些歧义。

cues.en: Remember,
cues.zh: 记住，

cues.en: the endpoints zero and one on the interval really correspond to the same point of the loop, as if to say that those endpoints need to be glued together if we're gonna faithfully map back to the loop.
cues.zh: 区间上的端点 0 和 1 其实对应环上的同一个点，也就是说，如果要忠实地映射回环，这两个端点需要粘合在一起。

cues.en: So all of the points on the left edge of the square like zero zero point one, zero zero point two, on and on and on, really represent the same pair of points on the loop as the corresponding coordinates on the right edge of the square one zero point one, one zero point two, on and on and on.
cues.zh: 所以正方形左边缘上的所有点，比如 (0, 0.1)、(0, 0.2) 等等，其实和正方形右边缘上对应的坐标 (1, 0.1)、(1, 0.2) 等等，代表的是环上同一对点。

cues.en: So for this square to represent the pairs of points on the loop in a unique way, we need to glue this left edge to the right edge.
cues.zh: 所以要让这个正方形唯一地表示环上的点对，我们需要把左边缘粘到右边缘上。

cues.en: I'll mark each edge with some arrows to remember how the edges need to be lined up.
cues.zh: 我会用一些箭头标记每条边，以便记住这些边需要如何对齐。

cues.en: Likewise, the bottom edge needs to be glued to the top edge since y coordinates of zero and one really represent the same second point in a given pair of points on the loop.
cues.zh: 同样地，底边需要粘合到顶边，因为坐标 0 和 1 实际上代表了环上给定点对中的同一个第二个点。

cues.en: If you bend the square to perform the gluing, first rolling it into a cylinder to glue the left and right edges,
cues.zh: 如果你把正方形弯曲来进行粘合，先把它卷成一个圆柱体来粘合左右两边，

cues.en: then gluing the ends of that cylinder which represent the top and bottom edges,
cues.zh: 然后粘合那个代表顶边和底边的圆柱体的两端，

cues.en: we get a torus better known as the surface of a donut.
cues.zh: 我们就得到了一个环面，也就是俗称的甜甜圈表面。

cues.en: Every individual point on this torus corresponds to a unique pair of points on the loop and likewise every pair of points on the loop corresponds to some unique point on this torus.
cues.zh: 这个环面上的每一个单独的点都对应于环上的一个唯一的分离点对，同样，环上的每一个点对也都对应于这个环面上的某个唯一的地。

cues.en: The torus is to pair of points on the loop what the x y plane is to pairs of points on the real number line.
cues.zh: 环面之于环上的点对，就像 xy 平面之于实数轴上的点对。

cues.en: The key property of this association
cues.zh: 这种对应关系的关键属性

cues.en: is that it's continuous both ways, meaning if you nudge any point on the torus by just a tiny amount, it corresponds to only a very slight nudge to the pair of points on the loop and vice versa.
cues.zh: 是它在双方向上都是连续的，这意味着如果你把环面上的任意点稍微 nudge 一小下，它只对应于环上点对的微小 nudge，反之亦然。

cues.en: So if the torus is the natural shape for ordered pairs of points on the loop, what's the natural shape for unordered pairs?
cues.zh: 所以，如果环面是环上有序点对的自然形态，那么无序点对的自然形态是什么呢？

cues.en: After all, the whole reason we're doing this is to show that two distinct pairs of points on the loop share a midpoint and are the same distance apart.
cues.zh: 毕竟，我们做这一切的全部原因是为了证明环上两对不同的点共享一个中点并且间距相等。

cues.en: But if we consider a pair a b to be distinct from b a, then that would trivially give us two separate pairs which have the same midpoint and distance apart.
cues.zh: 但是，如果我们认为点对 a b 不同于 b a，那就会轻而易举地得到两对具有相同中点和间距的独立点对。

cues.en: That's like saying you can always find a rectangle so long as you consider any pair of points to be a rectangle,
cues.zh: 这就像说，只要把任意一对点都当作矩形，就总能找到矩形，

cues.en: not helpful.
cues.zh: 这没什么用。

cues.en: So let's think about this. Let's think about how to represent unordered pairs of points looking back at our unit square.
cues.zh: 那我们来想想。回到单位正方形，想想如何表示无序点对。

cues.en: We need to say that the coordinates 0.2,
cues.zh: 我们需要说明，坐标 0.2、

cues.en: represent the same pair as 0.3,
cues.zh: 表示的是和 0.3、
0.2 相同的点对

cues.en: or that 0.5,
cues.zh: 或者说 0.5、

cues.en: really represents the same thing as 0.7,
cues.zh: 实际上表示的和 0.7、
0.5 是同一个东西。

cues.en: And in general, any coordinates x y has to represent the same thing as y x.
cues.zh: 一般来说，任意坐标 x y 都必须和 y x 表示同一个东西。

cues.en: Once again, we capture this idea by gluing points together when they're supposed to represent the same pair,
cues.zh: 我们再一次通过把本应表示同一点对的点粘合起来，来体现这个想法，

cues.en: which in this case requires folding the square over diagonally.
cues.zh: 在这个情况下，就是沿对角线把正方形折起来。

cues.en: Now notice this diagonal line, the crease of the fold.
cues.zh: 现在注意这条对角线，也就是折痕。

cues.en: It represents all pairs of points that look like x x, meaning the pairs which are really just a single point written twice.
cues.zh: 它表示所有形如 x x 的点对，也就是其实只是同一个点写了两次的点对。

cues.en: Right now it's marked with a red line and you should remember it. It will become important to know where all of these pairs like x x live.
cues.zh: 现在它用红线标出，你要记住它。知道所有形如 x x 的点对在哪里会很重要。

cues.en: But we still have some arrows to glue together here. We need to glue that bottom edge to the right edge
cues.zh: 但我们这里还有一些箭头要粘合。我们需要把底边粘到右边

cues.en: and the orientation with which we do this is gonna be important.
cues.zh: 而且粘合时的方向会很重要。

cues.en: Points towards the left of the bottom edge have to be glued to points towards the bottom of the right edge and points towards the right of the bottom edge have to be glued to points towards the top of the right edge.
cues.zh: 底边靠左的点必须粘到右边靠下的点，底边靠右的点必须粘到右边靠上的点。

cues.en: It's weird to think about, right? Go ahead pause and ponder this for a moment.
cues.zh: 这想想挺奇怪的，对吧？不妨暂停一下，仔细琢磨琢磨。

cues.en: The trick which is kind of clever is to make a diagonal cut which we need to remember to glue back in just a moment.
cues.zh: 这个技巧挺巧妙：沿对角线剪开，不过要记住，待会儿还得把它粘回去。

cues.en: After that, we can glue the bottom and the right like so.
cues.zh: 然后，我们像这样把底边和右边粘起来。

cues.en: But notice the orientation of the arrows here. To glue back what we just cut, we don't simply connect the edges of this rectangle to get a cylinder.
cues.zh: 但注意这里箭头的方向。要把刚剪开的部分粘回去，并不是简单地把这个矩形的两条边接起来做成圆柱面。

cues.en: We have to make a twist.
cues.zh: 我们得扭一下。

cues.en: Doing this in three d space, the shape we get is a Mobius strip. Isn't that awesome?
cues.zh: 在三维空间里这样做，得到的形状就是莫比乌斯带。是不是很酷？

cues.en: Evidently, the surface which represents all pairs of unordered points on the loop is the Mobius strip.
cues.zh: 显然，表示环上所有无序点对的曲面就是莫比乌斯带。

cues.en: And notice the edge of the strip shown here in red represents the pairs of points that look like x x, those which are really just a single point listed twice.
cues.zh: 注意这里用红色标出的带边，表示形如 x x 的点对，也就是同一个点被列了两次。

cues.en: The Mobius strip is to unordered pairs of points on the loop what the x y plane is to pairs of real numbers.
cues.zh: 莫比乌斯带之于环上的无序点对，就像 xy 平面之于实数对。

cues.en: That totally blew my mind when I first saw it.
cues.zh: 我第一次看到时，彻底被震撼到了。

cues.en: Now with this fact that there is a continuous one to one association
cues.zh: 现在，有了这样一个事实：存在一种连续的一一对应

cues.en: between unordered pairs of points on the loop and individual points on this Mobius strip,
cues.zh: 在环上的无序点对与这个莫比乌斯带上的各个点之间，

cues.en: we can solve the inscribed rectangle problem.
cues.zh: 我们就能解决内接矩形问题。

cues.en: Remember, we had defined the special kind of graph in three d space where the loop was sitting in the x y plane.
cues.zh: 还记得吗，我们定义过三维空间中的一种特殊图形，其中环位于 xy 平面上。

cues.en: For each pair of points, you consider their midpoint m which lives on the x y plane and their distance d apart and you plot a point which is exactly d units above m.
cues.zh: 对每一对点，考虑它们位于 xy 平面上的中点 m，以及它们相距的距离 d，然后在 m 正上方 d 个单位处画一个点。

cues.en: Because of the continuous one to one association between pairs of points on the loop and the Mobius strip,
cues.zh: 由于环上的点对与莫比乌斯带之间存在连续的一一对应关系，

cues.en: this gives us a natural map from the mobius strip onto this surface in three d space.
cues.zh: 这给了我们一个从莫比乌斯带到三维空间中这个曲面的自然映射。

cues.en: For every point on the mobius strip
cues.zh: 对于莫比乌斯带上的每个点，

cues.en: consider the pair of points on the loop that it represents,
cues.zh: 考虑它所代表的环上的那一对点，

cues.en: then plug that pair of points into the special function.
cues.zh: 然后把这对点代入那个特殊函数。

cues.en: And here's the key point, when pairs of points on the loop are extremely close together, the output of the function is right above the loop itself.
cues.zh: 关键点在于，当环上的点对彼此非常接近时，函数的输出正好位于环本身的正上方。

cues.en: And in the extreme case of pairs of points like x x, the output of the function is exactly on the loop.
cues.zh: 而在像 x x 这样的点对的极端情形下，函数的输出恰好落在环上。

cues.en: Since points on this red edge of the Mobius strip correspond to pairs like x x, when the Mobius strip is mapped onto this surface,
cues.zh: 由于莫比乌斯带这条红色边缘上的点对应于像 x x 这样的点对，当莫比乌斯带被映射到这个曲面上时，

cues.en: it must be done in such a way that the edge of the strip gets mapped right onto that loop in the x y plane.
cues.zh: 就必须让带的边缘正好映射到 xy 平面中的那个环上。

cues.en: But if you stand back and think about it for a moment, considering the strange shape of the Mobius strip, there is no way to glue its edge to something two dimensional without forcing the strip to intersect itself.
cues.zh: 但如果你退后一步想一下，考虑到莫比乌斯带奇怪的形状，要想把它的边缘粘到某个二维对象上，就必然迫使这条带与自身相交。

cues.en: Since points of the Mobius strip represent pairs of points on the loop, if the strip intersects itself during this mapping,
cues.zh: 由于莫比乌斯带上的点表示环上的点对，如果这条带在这个映射过程中与自身相交，

cues.en: it means that there are at least two distinct pairs of points that correspond to the same output on this surface,
cues.zh: 这意味着至少有两个不同的点对对应于这个曲面上的同一个输出，

cues.en: which means they share a midpoint and are the same distance apart,
cues.zh: 也就是说它们共享同一个中点，并且彼此间距相同，

cues.en: which in turn means that they form a rectangle.
cues.zh: 这反过来意味着它们构成一个矩形。

cues.en: And that's the proof, or at least if you're willing to trust me in saying that you can't glue the edge of a Mobius strip to a plane without forcing it to intersect itself, then that's the proof.
cues.zh: 这就是证明，或者说，如果你愿意相信我说的——你无法在不强迫莫比乌斯带与自身相交的情况下，把它的边缘粘到一个平面上——那么这就是证明。

cues.en: This fact is intuitively clear looking at the Mobius strip, but in order to make it rigorous, you basically need to start developing the field of topology.
cues.zh: 这个事实在直观上看莫比乌斯带就很清楚，但要让它严谨，你基本上需要开始发展拓扑学这个领域。

cues.en: In fact, for any of you who have a topology class in your future,
cues.zh: 事实上，如果你们中有人将来要上拓扑课，

cues.en: going through the exercise of trying to justify this is a good way to gain an appreciation
cues.zh: 试着去论证这一点是个好练习，能让你体会到

cues.en: for why topologists
cues.zh: 为什么拓扑学家

cues.en: choose to make certain definitions.
cues.zh: 选择做出某些定义。

cues.en: And I want you to take note of something here. The reason for talking about the torus and the Mobius strip was not because we were playing around with construction paper or because we were daydreaming about deforming a coffee mug.
cues.zh: 我想让你们注意一件事。我们谈论环面和莫比乌斯带，并不是因为我们在玩手工纸，也不是因为我们在幻想把咖啡杯变形。

cues.en: They came up as a natural way to understand pairs of points on a loop, and that's something that we needed to solve a concrete problem.
cues.zh: 它们是一种自然的方式，用来理解环上的一对点，而这是我们解决一个具体问题所需要的。
